q: 1. The water obtained from the tube wells is known as .............
explain: Water found below the earth's surface, such as that tapped by tube wells or open wells, is classified as sub-surface or ground water.

q: 2. The vertical wells provided along the banks of a river to draw ground water in dry season are called .............
explain: Infiltration wells are vertical structures sunk along river banks to tap the sub-surface flow, especially useful when surface levels drop.

q: 3. The layers such as sand and gravel which allow the water to pass through them are known as .............
explain: All three terms refer to geological formations that have sufficient porosity and permeability to transmit water.

q: 4. The yield of the well is measured on .............
explain: Yield is a flow rate, usually expressed in volume units per unit of time (cubic meters per hour or liters per hour).

q: 5. When lead is present in water, it .............
explain: Lead is a toxic metal that is generally colorless and tasteless in water but poses severe health risks (plumbism).

q: 6. The commercial osmoscope is graduated with pO values from .............
explain: The pO value (odour intensity) on an osmoscope typically ranges from 0 (no odour) to 5 (very strong odour).

q: 7. Odours and taste may results due to the presence of .............
options: Micro organisms either dead or alive
dissolved gases such as oxygen, carbon dioxide, methane etc.
minerals substance such as sodium chloride iron compounds etc
explain: Tastes and odours in water can be biological (algae/bacteria), gaseous ($H_2S$, $CH_4$), or chemical (salts/metals) in origin.

q: 8. The maximum permissible turbidity for domestic supplies, on silica scale is .............
explain: For drinking water, turbidity should ideally be less than 5 NTU/ppm and should not exceed 10 ppm for aesthetic and disinfection efficiency reasons.

q: 9. High turbidity of water can be determined by .............
explain: The Jackson Turbidimeter is a visual method used for measuring high turbidity (usually above 25 units) based on the length of a light path through the water.

q: 10. The maximum permissible chloride supplies in water for domestic supplies should not exceed .............
explain: A chloride concentration above 250 ppm gives water a salty taste and can increase the rate of corrosion in metal pipes.

q: 11. When the pH value of water is ............. the water is said to be acidic.
explain: A pH of 7 is neutral; values below 7 indicate acidity, while values above 7 indicate alkalinity.

q: 12. Copper sulphate is the most common chemical used for controlling .............
explain: Copper sulphate ($CuSO_4$) is a potent algicide used to prevent algae blooms in reservoirs.

q: 13. The detention time for an ordinary plain sedimentation tank is .............
explain: Detention time is the theoretical time water stays in the tank. For plain sedimentation, it typically ranges from 4 to 8 hours.

q: 14. In a plain sedimentation tank, under normal conditions, impurities are removed upto .............
explain: Well-designed sedimentation tanks can remove about 70% of suspended silt and clay from raw water.

q: 15. The under drainage system in a rapid sand filters .............
options: receives and collects the filtered water
allows back washing for cleaning the filter
explain: In rapid sand filters, the under-drainage system is multifunctional: it collects filtered water during the run and distributes high-pressure wash water and air during the cleaning (backwash) cycle.

q: 16. Rate of filtration of a slow sand filter ranges from .............
explain: Slow sand filters operate at a very low rate, usually between 100 to 200 liters per hour per square meter of filter area.

q: 17. The yield of a rapid sand filter is ............. to that of slow sand filter.
explain: Rapid sand filters have filtration rates (3000-6000 L/h/m²) that are roughly 30 times higher than slow sand filters (100-200 L/h/m²).

q: 18. Cleaning period for a rapid sand filter is taken as .............
explain: Because they operate at much higher rates, rapid sand filters clog quickly and typically need cleaning every 1 to 3 days.

q: 19. Rapid sand filter can remove turbidity from water upto an extend of .............
explain: Rapid sand filters are designed to handle and remove higher levels of turbidity compared to slow sand filters, provided pre-treatment is correct.

q: 20. Pressure filters are best suited for .............
explain: Due to their high rate and enclosed design, they are ideal for swimming pools, industrial sites, and small colonies.

q: 21. The treatment of water with only chlorine is known as .............
explain: Plain chlorination is the process of adding chlorine to raw water that has not received any other treatment (like filtration or sedimentation).

q: 22. The amount of chlorine used for plain chlorination of water is about .............
explain: Plain chlorination typically requires around 0.5 mg/L (ppm) to achieve proper disinfection in relatively clean raw water.

q: 23. The percentage of chlorine in fresh bleaching power is .............
explain: Commercial 'fresh' bleaching powder usually contains about 30% to 35% available chlorine.

q: 24. The temporary hardness in water is caused due to the salts like .............
explain: Temporary (carbonate) hardness is caused by bicarbonates and carbonates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 25. In order to prevent water to flow back opposite direction, we shall use a
explain: Reflux valves are used specifically to ensure water flows in the intended direction only, preventing reversal.

q: 26. Of the total content of water on globe the available quantity for use is less than
explain: While much of the globe is water, most is saline or frozen; accessible freshwater for human use is a tiny fraction of the total.

q: 27. Turbidity for domestic water is undesirable because it
explain: Turbidity makes water look cloudy or 'muddy,' which makes it visually unappealing (unaesthetic) to consumers.

q: 28. The standard unit of turbidity is produced when
options: 1 mg of silicon dioxide in 1 litre of distilled water
1 mg of platinum in 1 litre of distilled water
1 mg of sodium chloride in 1 litre of distilled water
1 mg of cobalt in 1 litre of distilled water
explain: One unit of turbidity is traditionally defined as the turbidity produced by 1 mg of fine silica ($SiO_2$) in 1 liter of pure water.

q: 29. Units of turbidity are
explain: NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units) is the standard modern unit for turbidity measurement.

q: 30. Water for domestic use should have
explain: While 'no smell' is ideal, the practical standard for domestic water is that it must be 'inoffensive' to the consumer.

q: 31. Due to the photosynthetic activity of algae pH of pools of water
explain: During the day, algae remove $CO_2$ for photosynthesis, which reduces acidity and causes the pH to rise.

q: 32. In a D.O. test oxygen is replaced by equivalent in
explain: In the Winkler method, dissolved oxygen reacts to eventually release an equivalent amount of iodine, which is then titrated.

q: 33. One of the important elements responsible for eutrophication is ...........
explain: Phosphates are often the 'limiting nutrient' in freshwater systems. Excess phosphorus from detergents or fertilizers is a primary driver of rapid algal blooms and eutrophication.

q: 34. Absolutely soft waters are required for ...........
explain: Boilers require soft water to prevent the formation of hard scales (calcium/magnesium deposits) on heat-exchange surfaces, which reduce efficiency and can cause boiler explosions.

q: 35. A water borne disease is ...........
explain: Water-borne diseases are caused by drinking contaminated water. Dysentery (amoebic or bacillary) is a classic example of a disease spread via the fecal-oral route through water.

q: 36. Oily odour and taste producing substances are produced by ...........
explain: Certain types of algae (like Diatoms or Synura) release oils and decomposition products that impart distinct fishy, oily, or grassy tastes and odors to water.

q: 37. A factor affecting domestic demand is ...........
options: dead end system or reticulation system of network of pipes
water supplied is soft or hard
explain: Climate significantly affects domestic use; water consumption is much higher in hot, dry climates for bathing, gardening, and cooling compared to cold regions.

is not deeper than a shallow well
is formed by just tapping the nearest aquifer to the ground
explain: Deep wells tap confined aquifers below impervious layers. These sources are more reliable and provide a more constant discharge compared to shallow wells which fluctuate with rainfall.

q: 39. A river intake may be situated on ...........
options: the convex side of a curved course
explain: A straight reach of the river is preferred for intakes to avoid the erosion found on concave banks and the silting/deposition found on convex banks.

q: 40. Detention time in a flash mixer is ...........
explain: Flash mixing is a very rapid process intended to disperse the coagulant uniformly throughout the water, typically taking less than a minute.

q: 41. Schmutzdecke will be formed in ...........
options: both slow sand and pressure filters
explain: Schmutzdecke (dirty skin) is a biological layer of algae, bacteria, and protozoa that forms on the surface of a Slow Sand Filter and is responsible for its high efficiency.

q: 42. Fine sand is used as media in case of ...........
options: both rapid and slow sand filters
explain: Slow sand filters use a finer grade of sand ($D_{10}$ approx. 0.2 to 0.3 mm) to ensure effective filtration at very low flow rates.

q: 43. Effluent from this unit requires no other treatment other than disinfection ...........
options: both rapid and slow sand filters
explain: Slow sand filters are so efficient at removing bacteria (98-99%) and turbidity that the treated water is generally safe enough to require only minimal chlorination.

q: 44. A heavy metal capable of disinfecting is ...........
explain: Silver has oligodynamic properties, meaning tiny amounts can kill bacteria. It is sometimes used for small-scale or specialized disinfection.

q: 45. Residual chlorine is given out when ...........
options: chlorine required for disinfection and oxidation of organic matter is less than applied chlorine
chlorine required is more than that supplied
chlorine applied is just sufficient to that required
explain: Residual Chlorine = Applied Chlorine - Chlorine Demand. It is the amount left over to provide continued protection against re-contamination.

q: 46. Disinfection ability of a chemical depends on ...........
options: concentration of disinfectant x time of concentration
explain: This is known as the 'Ct' concept (Concentration x Time). A lower concentration requires a longer contact time to achieve the same level of disinfection.

q: 47. Super chlorination is done ...........
options: when no other treatment is resorted to
explain: Super chlorination involves applying a very high dose of chlorine (e.g., 5-15 mg/l) during emergencies like disease outbreaks to ensure total destruction of pathogens.

q: 48. An advantage of ozone over chlorine for disinfection is it (ozone) ............
options: leaves sufficient chemical to guard against post contamination
explain: Ozone acts as a strong oxidizing agent that can improve the taste and odor of water by breaking down organic compounds, whereas chlorine can sometimes leave a medicinal taste.

q: 49. Iron and manganese can be removed from water by ............
explain: Oxidation (often through aeration or chemical addition) converts soluble iron and manganese into insoluble forms that can then be removed by filtration.

q: 50. Besides calcium and magnesium, hardness is also caused because of salts of ............
explain: While Ca and Mg are the main culprits, polyvalent metallic cations like Strontium (Sr2+), Iron, and Manganese also contribute to total hardness.

q: 51. The solubility of CaCO3 in pure water at 20°C is ............
explain: The theoretical solubility of calcium carbonate in pure water at standard room temperature is approximately 17 mg/l.

q: 52. The solubility of Mg(OH)2 in pure water at 20°C is ............
explain: Magnesium hydroxide is even less soluble than calcium carbonate, with a solubility of about 9 mg/l at 20°C.

q: 53. When the source of water is a reservoir on a mountain slope and the city is in plains then the system of distribution is ............
options: gravity system for a part and pumping for the remaining
explain: A gravity system is used when the source is at a higher elevation than the distribution area, allowing water to flow naturally without pumps.

q: 54. 'Mass action' during sedimentation is the property of ............
options: settling of a particle along with the neighbouring particle
explain: In hindered or zone settling, particles are so concentrated that they settle as a single mass or 'blanket' rather than individually.
